plates.side_label: 1879–1956 TIMELINE · FLEMMING MITOSIS, BOVERI/SUTTON, STEVENS XX/XY, MORGAN/STURTEVANT FLY ROOM & TJIO/LEVAN 46 HUMAN CHROMOSOMES
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1879–1883 (Walther Flemming stains salamander chromosomes to discover chromatin and mitosis in Kiel; Edouard van Beneden discovers chromosome halving in meiosis) · 1902–1905 (Theodor Boveri and Walter Sutton propose the Chromosome Theory of Inheritance; Nettie Stevens discovers X and Y sex chromosomes in mealworm beetles) · May 1910 – Jan 1913 (Thomas Hunt Morgan discovers X-linked inheritance in a white-eyed male Drosophila at Columbia; 19-year-old Alfred Sturtevant publishes the first linear chromosome map, winning Morgan the 1933 Nobel Prize).

teach_overlay.label: 1879–1956 CHROMOSOME & GENE-MAPPING TIMELINE · FLEMMING, SUTTON/BOVERI, STEVENS, MORGAN, STURTEVANT & TJIO/LEVAN (2N=46)
teach_overlay.detail: Animated timeline (1879 → 1956) alongside Tjio & Levan (1956 Hereditas 42: 1–6) 46-chromosome human karyotype (22 autosome pairs + XX/XY) and Sturtevant's centimorgan genetic map
teach_overlay.scale: from aniline fabric dye on salamander gills in Germany to rotting bananas in New York milk bottles, scientists proved that our entire hereditary blueprint rides on forty-six microscopic threads
